title: Abdul El-Sayed projected to win Michigan Democratic Senate primary, defeating Haley Stevens
facts: Abdul El-Sayed defeated Representative Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary.
Abdul El-Sayed previously served as a health official in Michigan.
Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez endorsed Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan primary.
Independent Senator Bernie Sanders endorsed Abdul El-Sayed in the primary campaign.
Michigan State Senator Mallory McMorrow withdrew from the Democratic Senate primary race in July.
Haley Stevens has represented Michigan in the US House of Representatives since 2019.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer recruited Haley Stevens to enter the Senate race.
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer endorsed Haley Stevens in the Senate primary race.
Democratic Senator Gary Peters announced he would not seek reelection to the Senate in Michigan.
Abdul El-Sayed will face Republican nominee Mike Rogers in the November general election.
Mike Rogers ran unopposed in Michigan's Republican Senate primary.
Mike Rogers previously lost to Senator Elissa Slotkin in Michigan's 2024 Senate race.
Senator Kirsten Gillibrand serves as the chair of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.
Republicans held 53 seats in the United States Senate at the time of the primary.
Abdul El-Sayed campaigned on progressive policies including the implementation of Medicare for All.
